Alerts
When something needs you and this window isn\'t in front, an alert comes from the tray. Click it to come back here.
This desktop has no tray that this app can use, so no alert can appear. The window\'s title counts what needs you instead.
This computer\'s key and sign-in tokens
There\'s no key on this computer yet. One is made when it pairs.
It\'s in your system\'s keychain, so it isn\'t lying readable on the disk or in a copy of your home folder. Other programs running as you can still ask the keychain for it while you\'re logged in.

Your system\'s keychain is locked or isn\'t running, so the key is in a private file in this app\'s folder for now. This computer still connects. The key moves to the keychain when you try again with it unlocked, or the next time this app starts.

The key is in a private file in this app\'s folder, because this app can\'t reach a keychain here. On Linux it needs secret-tool (the libsecret-tools package) and a running keychain such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet. It then moves there the next time this app starts.
Your system\'s keychain didn\'t give the key back correctly, so it stays in a private file in this app\'s folder. This computer still connects, and this app tries again the next time it starts.
The key is in a private file in this app\'s folder, because HYPERNOVA_CLIENT_KEYCHAIN is off.
Any program running as you can read that file, and so can anyone with a copy of your home folder, unless the disk is encrypted.

The sign-in token for each server you pair is in the keychain too, so a copy of this app\'s folder can\'t connect as this computer. Other programs running as you can still ask the keychain for them while you\'re logged in.

Your system\'s keychain is locked or isn\'t running, so a sign-in token is in a private file in this app\'s folder for now. This computer still connects. The token moves to the keychain when you try again with it unlocked, or the next time this app starts.
The sign-in tokens are in a private file in this app\'s folder, because this app can\'t reach a keychain here.

Your system\'s keychain didn\'t give a sign-in token back correctly, so it stays in a private file in this app\'s folder. This computer still connects, and this app tries again the next time it starts.
The sign-in tokens are in a private file in this app\'s folder, because HYPERNOVA_CLIENT_KEYCHAIN is off.
A copy of that file can connect as this computer until you unpair it on your server. Any program running as you can read it too.
Try again

Waiting for your keychain
The sign-in token for %1$s is in your system\'s keychain, and the keychain is locked or isn\'t running. Nothing is lost and you don\'t need to pair again. Unlock it, then try again.

Your system\'s keychain has no sign-in token for %1$s. If it\'s only locked, unlock it and try again. If the keychain was reset or this app\'s folder moved, the token is gone, and you\'ll need to pair again.
The sign-in token for %1$s is in your system\'s keychain, and this app can\'t reach a keychain here. On Linux it needs secret-tool (the libsecret-tools package). Install it and start this app again.
The sign-in token for %1$s is in your system\'s keychain, and HYPERNOVA_CLIENT_KEYCHAIN is off, so this app won\'t ask it. Remove that setting and start this app again.
Forget %1$s
Forgetting a server means pairing it again. Its token is removed from the keychain as soon as the keychain lets it.
Alerts only come while this app is running. Closing the window ends it, so minimize the window instead.
